subject: Secure SDLC intake: evidence mapping, shortlived keys, and canary rollback plan
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@deltabank.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: security-assess@deltabank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence intake request — SDLC sampling, CI retention, and key rotation

Chloe,

Thanks for agreeing to help DeltaBank's assessor team with the intake. We need a compact evidence bundle to validate your SDLC controls for the SIG+CAIQ intake. To keep this scoped for assessment, could you provide the following by next Wednesday (2028-11-15):

- A short one-page narrative describing your change management flow and emergency patch authority (who can approve out-of-window deploys).
- Three sample PRs (merge histories) from the last six months that include reviewer comments, approvals, and CI run IDs.
- CI run logs (redacted) showing artifact signing or build provenance for the sampled PRs.
- Keystore/credential rotation logs for the last 90 days (keystore-change-ids, rotation dates).
- Evidence of shortlived credential use: ephemeral token issuance records and sampling of their expiration policy.
- Deploy/rollback traces for one canary deploy and one hotfix (including who approved the rollback).

We prefer encrypted bundles uploaded to our SFTP (details below). If you have a SOC2 mapping or control matrix that maps these artifacts to SIG/CAIQ controls, please include it but redacted where necessary.

SFTP host: sftp.assess.deltabank.com
Upload path: /incoming/delta/2028-11-15
Contact: Tom Hayes (tom.hayes@deltabank.com)

Appreciate a short mutual action plan (owners + dates) so we can confirm expectations with the assessor. If any of this is out of scope or requires an alternate delivery mechanism (e.g., secure Drive link + NDA), flag that.

Thanks,
Tom Hayes
Lead Assessor — Third Party Risk
DeltaBank

Attachments: sdlc_evidence_checklist.pdf (10kb stub)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@deltabank.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Nov 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence intake request — SDLC sampling, CI retention, and key rotation

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll take this on. High level plan and owners below:

- One-pager change narrative (owner: Chloe) — draft by 2028-11-13.
- PR/CI artifacts sampling (owner: Irene) — pick 3 PRs, redact PII, package logs by 2028-11-14.
- Keystore rotation & ephemeral token samples (owner: Marissa) — extract rotation events and token issuance trace by 2028-11-14.
- Deploy/rollback traces (owner: Irene + Marissa) — include a canary and a hotfix, include approver audit trail by 2028-11-15.

Delivery: we can produce an encrypted ZIP and upload to your SFTP path. Alternative: share a time-limited, auditor-only Drive link and an MD5 checksum. We will not include any customer PII in the bundle; we'll redact commit messages if they contain usernames or sensitive IDs.

Irene, Marissa — can you confirm the PR samples you plan to include and whether any of the CI runs need extra redaction (e.g., tests referencing customer IDs)?

Tom — attaching our internal scope list for transparency (sdlc_evidence_scope_list.pdf). We'll include related console trace links for traceability, and a small manifest that maps each file to SIG/CAIQ control references.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Head of Compliance Programs (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sdlc_evidence_scope_list.pdf (8kb stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@deltabank.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Nov 2028 13:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence intake request — SDLC sampling, CI retention, and key rotation

Chloe / Marissa / Tom —

Quick clarifications so we target the right artifacts:

1) For PRs, do you need full commit signatures (GPG) or is the GitHub PR approval+merge record sufficient? We have both for tagged releases but not for every hotfix.
2) CI logs: we will redact any test artifacts and customer identifiers. Do you require raw logs or condensed run transcripts with step names and exit statuses?
3) Keystore rotation: we can provide a CSV of rotation events (rotation_id, key_id, actor, reason, timestamp) but cannot export private key material (obvious).
4) Ephemeral tokens: policy doc + sample issuance events (token_id, issued_at, expires_at, requester_role).

Proposed sampling approach (minimizes noise):
- Three releases (major/minor): one scheduled release, one quick minor, one emergency hotfix.
- For each release: PR thread PDF (first comment -> approvals -> merge), CI run transcript (redacted), artifact checksum and build id.
- Canary deploy trace: rollout event, metrics check snapshot, canary evaluation decision, rollback event (if any) and approver signatures.

We'll produce a small manifest CSV that maps each file to the control references (SIG: SDLC-1/SDLC-2; CAIQ: DevOps.3 etc.). Estimated bundle size ~12–30MB.

If that approach is acceptable I'll start assembling and will upload an encrypted bundle to sftp.assess.deltabank.com as requested. If you prefer Drive, please share a document-level NDA and an access window.

Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Applied ML
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none (will attach bundle after compilation)

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@deltabank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Nov 2028 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence intake request — SDLC sampling, CI retention, and key rotation

Irene / Chloe —

That sampling approach works for us. A couple of quick notes:

- PR approvals + merge record are sufficient; full GPG signatures are nice-to-have but not required.
- CI transcripts with step names and exit statuses work — no need for raw logs unless there is a specific failing step we ask to follow up on.
- The CSV rotation event export is exactly what we need; please include the key type (e.g., RSA-2048, pkcs11-hsm) in the metadata column.
- For the encrypted ZIP, please use AES-256 and share the passphrase with my team via an out-of-band channel (signal or our vendor key exchange).

Also: can you include a short one-page change narrative that explicitly states the emergency patch authority matrix (roles + escalation path)? That helps our reviewer sign off faster.

We'll watch for the upload to /incoming/delta/2028-11-15 and circle back with follow-ups by Friday (2028-11-18) if anything needs clarification.

Thanks again — looking forward to the manifest.

Tom Hayes
Lead Assessor — Third Party Risk
DeltaBank

Attachment: sftp_instructions.txt (1kb stub)
